cities.d: Belgium's capital and the unofficial capital of the EU. Nice historic centre and several museums of interest. One of the most multicultural cities in Europe.

x.around: Broadly speaking, it is strongly suggested not to drive near or within the R0. Most streets near the Grand-Place have been pedestrianised, and only taxi and delivery drivers can access that area. However, the outskirts of Brussels (especially the southern region like Ukkel) are not always served by buses or trams, so having a car might be useful there.

hidden.d: Guided tours not available. Presentations available for groups of 15 or more, booked in advance.

Small pavilion designed by Victor Horta and housing the monumental sculpture "The Human Passions" by Jef Lambeaux. A dispute between the creators and a scandal over the artwork's controversial erotic and religious iconography…
The museum building was designed as covered garage and parking for carriages and the first cars, but later converted into the present day museum.

Church in Italian Baroque style, with an unusual circular three-aisled layout and a central hexagonal dome to which 3 semicircular apes connect. The facade consists of 3 bays, delineated by ionic pilasters on high plinths.

n.en: Church of Our Lady of Bon Secours

hidden.d: Statue of Charles Buls, mayor of Brussels from 1881 until 1899. Charles was a prominent defender of equal rights, an intellectual, writer and widely regarded as the greatest mayor in modern history of the city.
The Sewer Museum invites you on an unusual trip into a very hidden side of Brussels but which is absolutely vital for the running of the city.

Museum centered on product design. The permanent collection is the Plasticarium, featuring 2,000 pieces, from everyday objects to pieces of art, from the post-modernism to pop-art, the utopia of everything in plastic.
The hall is a former covered marketplace in the middle of St. Gorik Square, and in use as event space and temporary exposition area.

x.intro: Brussels (French: Bruxelles, Dutch: Brussel) is the capital of Belgium and one of the three administrative regions within the country, together with Flanders and Wallonia. Apart from its role within its country, it is also an internationally important city, hosting numerous international institutions, and in particular the headquarters of NATO and the core institutions of the European Union.

must.d: Multimedia-guided tours in all official EU languages. Don't forget to bring an ID card/driver's license with you.
Guided tours not available. Presentations available for groups of 15 or more, booked in advance.
A short walk from the Grand-Place/Grote Markt is the Manneken Pis, a small bronze statue thought to represent the "irreverent spirit" of Brussels. This is a statue of a child urinating into a pool.
Surrounded by the city tower and a range of beautiful 300-year-old buildings. In the evening, lit by bright illumination, it is simply ravishing.

Unavoidable icon of Brussels and Belgium, important place for international tourism, unique creation in the history of architecture and emblematic vestige of the World Fair in Brussels (Expo 58) the Atomium continues to embody…

Several turn-of-the-century houses and manors can still be seen today, such as the Stoclet Palace, a , which was built between 1905 and 1909 on a design by Josef Hoffmann and contains mosaics and paintings by Gustav Klimt.
On 11 November 1922, exactly 4 years after the First World War ceasefire, the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier was inaugurated by king Albert I.
Recognizable as a copy of the Notre Dame cathedral in Paris, the cathedral of Brussels has a long history. A chapel dedicated to St.

n.de: Kathedrale St. Michael und St. Gudula
n.en: Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula
n.es: Catedral de San Miguel y Santa Gúdula de Bruselas
n.it: concattedrale di San Michele e Santa Gudula

next.d: Bordering Brussels to the east. Architecture from the 16th to 18th centuries, primarily interesting for history and architecture enthusiasts.
South-east of Brussels, on the outskirts of the Sonian Forest, a .
About south of Brussels. Visit where Wellington and Bluecher faced Napoleon for an ultimate battle that changed Europe's face forever. Further south, don't miss the Abbey of Villers-la-Ville.
About 10 south of Brussels. Visit the nature reserve with Galloway cattle (not in winter) so near to Brussels
About 35 NE of Brussels.
About 30 east of Brussels.
About 55 north of Brussels.
About 45 NW of Brussels.

x.safe: This might come as a shock to the uninitiated, but Brussels is increasingly dealing with the reputation of being a rather unsafe or uneasy city, at least by Western European standards. Though one can argue that it is partially bloated by the media and "word-of-mouth", Brussels has its share of safety issues. Violent crime is rather rare, however pickpocketing, vandalism and petty theft are common.

cities.d: Belgium's second largest city, with a giant cathedral, medieval streets and artistic heritage, and a great place for fashion.

x.around: The tram system operates with low-floor articulated units (refer to the above photo), mostly in tunnels under the centre, & older high-floor tramcars, mostly on ground-level routes.

hidden.d: A beautiful mixed gothic and baroque church formerly part of a nunnery. Noted for its Calvary monument. It is a short distance north of the Grote Maarkt on Zwartzustersstraat.
There are actually two of these. The old one is a 19th-century red brick building on the Britselei. The new one is a dominant, modern, white building in the south of Antwerp (Bolivarplaats).
This is the historical centre of town. The market square is surrounded by the typical medieval guild houses you find in most Flemish historical towns.
Museum devoted to graphics. Permanently Featuring works by Francisco Goya, Félicien Rops and Edvard Munch. There are also temporary exhibitions.
You can take a guided tour of the underground city of Antwerp. 90 minutes. Free with City Card.
Connects Hoogstraat, Oude Koornmarkt and Pelgrimsstraat. It is a real street, but only accessible through unassuming medieval front doors in the streets. The medieval equivalent of a gated community.
A sort of medieval monastery for women. The well-kept gardens are great photo opportunities.

x.intro: Antwerp (Dutch: Antwerpen, French: Anvers) is the capital of the eponymous province in the region of Flanders in Belgium. At a population of just over half a million people (2018), it is the second largest city in Belgium (after Brussels), and it has a major European port. Due to its long and culturally rich history, the city of Antwerp houses interesting historical buildings from different historical periods and numerous museums.

must.d: The home of 16th-century bookbinder and printer Christoffel Plantin. Regarded as one of the finest museums dedicated to printing in the world.
One of the most impressive and largest Gothic cathedrals in Northern Europe, built in 1351 it stands over 400 ft tall. It also houses some of Rubens' most famous paintings.
Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten boasts an excellent collection of paintings from the 15th century to the 20th century.

n.es: Museo Real de Bellas Artes de Amberes
n.it: Museo reale di belle arti di Anversa

must.d: The house of painter Peter Paul Rubens is now a museum of his life and artwork. Many of his paintings and artworks and his contemporaries are installed in the rooms, as well as furniture of his period.

Large museum that tells about Antwerp in the world. You can visit the building for free, with a very wide view across Antwerp on the rooftop. The viewing platform on the roof is accessible without a museum ticket.
One of the oldest zoos in the world, with over 4000 animals and lots of 19th-century design and architecture.

This is a rather small medieval castle on the banks of the river Schelde. It used to function as a city fortification and housed a naval museum. The Visitor Center and attraction The Antwerp Story are located here since 2021.

Unlike the cathedral, this is a Baroque church. With a safe and minimal exterior, you would not know the beautiful decorations (done by Rubens' studio) are inside. It is on the picturesque square Conscienceplein.

n.es: iglesia de San Carlos de Borromeo

next.d: (Brugge) — Very nice medieval town. Often called "Venice of the North", because of the many canals that flow through and under it.
The capital of Belgium and some say, the capital of Europe. Multicultural and multilingual. Unfortunately, some of the city's historic (medieval) centre was destroyed at the end of the 19th century…
A medieval town a bit like Bruges, with more emphasis on cathedrals and other big buildings. Great centre of medieval paintings exhibited in and around the cathedral of Sint-Baafs.
The regional capital of Wallonia.
Nearly as lively as Antwerp or Brussels is this college town, home to one of the world's oldest universities is here. Many hotels also cater to businessmen who find Brussels too expensive.
You can take a direct train to Amsterdam in the Netherlands. There is about one train an hour and it will take you about two hours to get there.
You can take a direct train to Rotterdam in the Netherlands. There is about one train an hour and it will take you about one hour to get there. Rotterdam is well known for its harbour.
You can go by train to this medieval city (change trains in Roosendaal).

x.safe: Most parts of Antwerp are safe, but some neighborhoods are to be avoided in the evening, especially the area around De Coninckplein and the neighborhoods of Borgerhout, Seefhoek and the Schipperskwartier. Still, these neighbourhoods have a very lively atmosphere and so are definitely worth a visit during the day.

cities.d: one of Europe's wealthiest cities in the 14th century, it is touristy yet still very authentic, medieval and quiet at night, with small guest houses and family businesses greatly outnumbering chain…

x.around: The historical centre is not so big and thus quite walkable (be sure to wear comfortable shoes). The only mode of public transport inside the city is bus. They are operated by the Flemish public transport company De Lijn. They frequent nearly all major points of interest plus the train station. Taxis on the market place and station cost about .

hidden.d: An amazing (private) art gallery with a Gothic cemetery in a subtropical garden located in the old Freemasons temple (1756-1882). 1,000 m² of art and mystery in Bruges' old city centre.
This brewery is the only remaining that's still brewing beer inside the city walls. It's also a beer museum and offers a tour of the beer making process.
Diamond museum has a large range of exhibits ranging from mining all the way to polishing and all the history in between. Everyday at 12:15 there is a live polishing demonstration.

The city has two teams playing soccer in First Division A, the Belgian top tier: Club Brugge KV and Cercle Brugge KSV. They share the Jan Breydel stadium, capacity 29,000, in Sint-Andries district 2 km west of the centre.

A house, an open studio where thoughts and ideas are born, a place where Beelprez can mix these thoughts and feelings in a symbolic language of forms, her soul, her calligraphy, her world, her language.

n.en: Simbolik - Open Studio and Expo of Nathalie Beelprez

hidden.d: Daily hot air balloon flights over the historic centre and its surroundings. The best way to enjoy the romance of Bruges, and its stunning views, from a few hundred metres up in a balloon basket.
In a quiet area of the city, a highly unusual church with octagonal tower built by the Adornes brothers, merchants of Italian extraction.

Passionate local storytellers offer tours in the medieval city center. No old-fashioned tour focussing solely on historical details, but engaging stories to bring the history to life. Reservations advised.

x.intro: Bruges (Dutch (local name): Brugge) is a picturesque city in Flanders, the northern part of Belgium. Once Europe's richest city, it is now both cosmopolitan and bourgeois in its compact size. It is mainly known for its exceptionally well-preserved historical centre (especially by Belgian standards), which draws over 400,000 tourists annually.

must.d: A fascinating church with architecture from the Romanesque and Gothic periods. In the east end of the church are very fine tombs of Charles the Bold and his daughter Mary of Burgundy, in contrasting Gothic and Renaissance styles,…
Known as 'The city museum of Fine Arts', it houses a collection of artworks that span several centuries (14th-20th), focusing mainly on works by painters who lived and worked in Bruges.
A beautiful church on the Burg square. It houses a relic: a vial of blood that is said to be that of Jesus - and was built in the Gothic style.

n.en: Basilica of the Holy Blood (Heilige Bloed Basiliek)
n.es: basílica de la Santa Sangre de Brujas

must.d: In the history, many women couldn't find a man, as men were more likely to die in accidents or in a war. Those women could "marry God" and become a beguine.
Sint-Janshospitaal contains a museum of six paintings by Hans Memling, within the early medieval hospital buildings.

This museum is a must-see for chocolate enthusiasts as it describes chocolate's transition from cocoa into chocolate. Its low-cost tasty exhibits make it well worth the time (and Belcolade's gently overt marketing).
Part of the second city ramparts of 1297. The current gate dates back to the beginning of the 15th century.
Just like the Smedenpoort, this gate is completely surrounded by water. Nowadays the gate is only used by pedestrians and cyclists.

next.d: is a small town near Bruges. A seasonal riverboat goes there on a cruise of 35 minutes each way. It's a very scenic trip, the landscapes are picturesque, and the village of Damme even more so.
is a charming small historic city just across the Netherlands border, where the Damse Vaart (Damme Canal) terminates.
(Ieper) is an important site of Great War battles, cemeteries, monuments and traditions such as the Last Post (every evening). Very popular among old veterans and young boys interested in wars.
(Oostende) is the monumental beach resort, called queen of the coastal cities resort. King Leopold II (1865-1909) built before his attention turned to inner-city Brussels to build his new capital.
is a beach resort with many fanciful buildings in the belle époque style. Residential streets are lined by many quaint houses.
Brussels and Antwerp are great tourist destinations in their own right, and very easy to reach by train (30 minutes to Ghent, 1 hr to Brussels and Antwerp).

cities.d: once one of Europe's largest cities, now a perfect mixture of Antwerp and Bruges: a cosy city with canals, yet with rich history and lively student population.

x.around: The centre of Ghent is quite small, so you can walk around on foot. However, the main station (Gent Sint-Pieters) is not in the city centre, but takes a walk of about half an hour. The best option is to take the tram, which takes you directly to the centre in 10 to 15 minutes.

hidden.d: Where the local graffiti artists are allowed to do their work. Although other around the town on buildings are of better quality and artistic value.
15th-century gate over the canal into the city. The canal used to connect the town to the North Sea but now stops at this gate which is framed by 1960s housing blocks.
This béguinage (begijnhof) has several streets.
An 1880 Art Deco pool restored in 2001, it that retains individual changing rooms. The old entrance is still there but the modern entrance is at the opposite end of the building.

n.en: Go Swimming at Badhuis Van Eyck

hidden.d: Known formerly as the Museum for History of Sciences, the University Museum has collections on archaeology, ethnography, morphology and other sciences. Has a botanical garden (with greenhouses) next to the museum.
It was founded in 1986, and its exhibits address the history of psychiatry in a permanent collection and through a series of half-yearly changing thematic exhibitions.

n.en: The Museum Dr. Guislain – a museum on the history of mental health

hidden.d: The Blaarmeersen offers multiple sports grounds, including a climbing wall (3.500m², one of the biggest in Europe), athletics track, BMW, openwater swimming (on Thursday 18h-20h), roller blading, skate track, sup, cycling track,…
This museum housed in a former industrial building brings industrial heritage to life by means of exhibitions, workshops and film Sundays. Industry, labour and textiles are seamlessly interwoven.

n.en: Museum of Industrial Archaeology and Textiles (MIAT)

x.intro: Ghent (Dutch: Gent, French: Gand) is a city in East Flanders in Belgium. Ghent is a city with a population of 265,000 in 2020, with rich history. During the Middle Ages, Ghent was one of the richest and most powerful cities in Europe. The impact of this rich past can be clearly seen when viewing the imposing architecture of churches and the houses of rich traders. The city centre is restored, and breathes the atmosphere of a thriving late-medieval city state.

must.d: Don't miss this cathedral. Rather unimpressive exterior of Romanesque, Gothic, and baroque architecture. However, the interior is filled with priceless paintings and sculptures, including the 24-panel altarpiece The Adoration of…
Built by Count Philip of Alsace, count of Flanders, soon after he returned from the Crusades in 1180 with images of similar crusader castles in the Holy Land.

n.es: Castillo de los Condes de Gante

must.d: A mixture of surviving Romanesque elements of the Flemish architectural style known as Schelde Gothic, the impressive 13th- to 15th-century church was paid for by Ghent's wealthy medieval merchants and guilds.
Modern arts museum located in NE corner of citadelpark. Cafe on site.

n.es: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Gante

must.d: The medieval harbour is a beautiful setting with many historic buildings, including the house of the Grain Weighers, the toll house, and the Guildhall of the Free Boatmen, fronting onto the river Leie.
With its strong socialist tradition, Ghent is laden with historic buildings testifying to power of the social-democratic movement.

There is a Gothic facade facing the street Hoogpoort and a Renaissance facade facing the street Botermarkt. (Botermarkt literally means butter market.) Indoors, there are different styles. The belfry is a .
This begijnhof (Béguinage) has several curved streets. Gates are off of Engelbert Van Arenbergstraat or Jan Roomsstraat.

next.d: famous for its canals and medieval heritage as well, is 20 minutes by train from Ghent
with Belgium's largest market square, is also 20 minutes away
attracts lots of day-trippers from Belgium. It was once part of Flanders, and its main street and city entrance gate still refer to Ghent.
a charming and historically important provincial city in West Flanders is 30 minutes away
Brussels, Mechelen and the seaside resort of Ostend are around 40 minutes away
are within 1.5 hours of train ride - either direct or with a quick change in Brussels
is an hour away by direct train
is very near and offers a great half-day trip to those who are interested in arts.

cities.d: a small city dominated by one of Europe's oldest universities. Beautiful historic centre and a lively nightlife.

x.around: The city has installed several new touristic road signs and city maps at several locations, which make getting around in the city a lot easier. Don't be afraid to ask people on the street for information, as they are usually very open and helpful towards tourists - some will even walk you to your destination.

hidden.d: This beguinage, the larger of the two in the town, is a .
A beautiful building, a valuable collection. Also has an interesting, huge sculpture of a dead beetle (Totem, by Jan Fabre) on a needle in front of it.
5 km south of the city
The city museum, at the Vanderkelenstraat, close to the Ladeuzeplein and the Bondgenotenlaan. It has a permanent collection of medieval and modern art, and regularly hosts temporary exhibitions.
It has Leuven's own "statue of Liberty", a 15-metre-high statue of the Virgin Mary overlooking the city from the park surrounding the abbey.
The small beguinage.

x.intro: Leuven (French: Louvain) is a flourishing and lively city of about 100,000 inhabitants (2018). It is the capital of the Belgian province of Flemish Brabant. It's a genuine university city which reflects in the streets. During the academic year (end of September until end of June) the city is full of young people, especially on weekdays. Sometimes it may seem that there are no other people living in the city.

must.d: A richly decorated Gothic building on the Grote Markt. The belfry is a .

St Peter’s Church is a historic parish church in Leven with origins dating back to the medieval period. The church suffered serious damage in both WW1 and WW2 and much of the current structure reflects later rebuilding.

next.d: an hour from Ghent and 80 min from Bruges.

x.safe: Leuven is a very safe and clean city, with very low crime records.

cities.d: second largest city of Wallonia, along a wide river, industrial cityscape with hiking and resorts in the nearby hills, it has a very strong, independent character and an exciting night-life.

x.around: Unlike most Belgian cities, Liège has no inner ring built along the path of the old city walls. Instead, the main streets were laid out along the old branches of the river, which makes their organisation a bit obscure.

hidden.d: A former fortified collegiate church with a 12th-century tower.
An ethnological museum hosted in an old convent.
It will be integrated into the future Museum Grand Curtius, but can now be visited separately.
Now a museum (Musée d’Ansembourg), is worth visiting for the well-preserved original interior.
An underground archaeological site with the remains of the three (successive) cathedrals on the site, as well as a building from Roman times.
Perron, and houses along the market square. The town hall, is an elegant classic building. It was built in 1714, during reconstruction after the French attacks in 1691.
Climb the imposing staircase of 373 steps framed by small houses and gardens, or opt for the smaller streets and stairways leading up to the Citadel's slopes.

x.intro: Liège (German: Lüttich, Dutch: Luik) is the largest city of Wallonia. This industrial city is actually quite green, with wide boulevards, an interesting, if a bit disorderly, mix of architecture from different periods, much greenery and picturesque riverbanks and hillsides. There are also quite a few museums and other points of interest, enough for at least a busy day trip.

must.d: It was the last of 7 "collégiales liégeoises" to be built, near the end of the 11th century. It is home to the masterwork of the Liège goldsmiths from the Middle Ages: the baptismal fonts from the old parish church of the…

Constructed between 1881 and 1884 as a Belgian defensive measure against Germany, Fort de Loncin was attacked during the Battle of Liège, the first battle of the invasion of Belgium during the First World War.

next.d: World War II Ardennes American Cemetery and Memorial commemorates the American soldiers who died in Northern Europe during WWII.
World War II Henri-Chapelle American Cemetery and Memorial is the final resting place for 7,992 American military lost during the drive into Germany.
is the pleasant town that gave its name to mineral spring resorts.
dates from Roman times, but its sights are mostly medieval.
in the Netherlands has an attractive old centre.
(Aix-la-Chapelle) in Germany is ranged around its cathedral, begun in 796 AD.

x.safe: Liège is generally a safe city during daytime. However, be cautious at night, especially if you are a woman. It is not recommended for women to walk alone in the evenings, as many foreign female students have been followed late at night. Robbery is rare, but harassment of single females occurs often. It is mostly verbal, but some travelers have been assaulted in off-downtown areas.

cities.d: a small medieval city with a nice historic district around the cathedral.

x.around: The city center is about 15 minutes walk from the train station. Mechelen is a very compact city, so you can reach most places on foot. There are a few bus routes through and radiating from the city centre in case you need them.

hidden.d: Hieronymus of Busleyden afforded himself this eponymous Court in a rich renaissance style, making it one of the most beautiful buildings in Mechelen.
Privately run museum where the owners, both watchmakers, give you a very interesting personal tour. Do come an hour before closing time to be able to have the full tour and explanations.
Another of the churches, is known for the two statues above the door, one of Saint Catherine and one of God the Father.
One of the 8 historic churches in Mechelen, with a notable Reubens painting/triptych "Adoration of the Magi". The painting of the crucifixion by Wauters is also very impressive.

This museum and memorial opened in 2012. It documents the history of the holocaust and human rights. The barracks (Dutch: kazerne) were a waiting place for Jews from all over Belgium and northern France.
Historically the refuge for the abbey in times of attack, it is now the home of De Wit, royal manufacturers of tapestry. There are guided visits on Saturday mornings at 1030.

n.en: Refuge of the Abbey of Tongerlo

hidden.d: Hands-on science museum for kids of all ages.

x.intro: Mechelen is a historically important city on the river Dyle in the centre of Flanders. It is a vibrant town, mixing trendy and traditional. Its carillon school is world-renowned, training students from all over the world in the art of playing carillons, sets of 24 or more bells hung in church towers. Shops downtown are often housed in buildings with the old-style Flemish architecture, but offer edgy fashions sure to appeal to the younger generation.

must.d: The largest of the 8 churches in Mechelen, with a high tower (though not as high as had been planned — construction stopped early due to lack of money).
The cathedral cutting across one end and the City Hall (a ) at the opposite end, with restaurants and cafes lining the sides between the two.

next.d: Major port town north of Mechelen, with a large shopping, diamond and fashion scene.
The lively and diverse national capital is only a short train ride away.
Nearly as lively as Antwerp or Brussels is this college town, home to one of the world's oldest universities is here. Many hotels also cater to businessmen who wish not to stay in Brussels.
Nearby small town with some medieval sights.

x.safe: While Mechelen used to have one of the highest crime rates in Flanders, it is safe to walk through Mechelen now. The city has improved much over the last years, especially in the tourist areas. You may want to keep out of the outskirts at night, though, but there is not much to do there anyway.

cities.d: has had the extraordinary privilege of having two sites inscribed on the List and one event on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

x.around: A free shuttle service runs between 07:00 and 21:00. The shuttles run along three circuits, all of which terminate at the train station Gare B. All run past Sainte Waudru and the Grand Place.

hidden.d: This museum is entirely dedicated to the crazy Ducasse celebrations that yearly take place in Mons. You will learn about the history of the event. The audio content is in French, English and Dutch.
Dates back to the 16th century and was built entirely out of bricks.
It was built near the current location of the belfry, and was moved on the Grand Place in the 13th century. The flamboyant Gothic building we see today dates from the 15th century.
Museum displaying contemporary art with interesting temporary exhibitions.
The centre of the historic town and the stage for the annual mock-battle of the Lumeçon.

x.intro: Mons (Dutch: Bergen, not to be confused with the namesake city in Norway) is the capital of the Belgian province of Hainaut, in the region of Wallonia. The town is a worthy place to base yourself for a multi-day exploration of the Hainaut region.

must.d: You can visit a silex mine dating back to the Neolithic period. This is a .

n.es: Minas neolíticas de sílex de Spiennes
n.fr: minières néolithiques de silex de Spiennes
n.it: Cave neolitiche di selce a Spiennes

must.d: Classified as a , dates from the 17th century and is the only Baroque-style belfry in Belgium.
Paradoxically a good specimen of Brabantic Gothic architecture.
Cuesmoise the house where he lived from August 1879 to October 1880, was saved from ruin in the 1970s and is now accessible to the public.
Museum devoted to the decorative arts from the period 1775 to 1825 located in the former building of the National Bank of Belgium. The items are in a wonderful condition.
The exhibits on display from the City of Mons give the visitors more insight in the two world wars that turned the 20th century upside down.

next.d: home to Pairi Daiza, a popular animal park north of Mons on the way to Ath.

cities.d: capital of Wallonia, at the confluence of Sambre and Meuse with the Citadel.

x.around: The layout of the city is complex and navigation is not easy, a detailed map is highly recommended. OpenStreetMap has moderate coverage of Namur. ===By foot=== Namur is not really a big city and is perfect to discover on foot. With good hiking shoes, light gear and favorable weather it is the most interesting, cheapest and most pleasant option.

hidden.d: On a rainy day worth a visit. It has recorded guiding in English and a collection of Medieval and Renaissance Christian art.
Mostly displaying artifacts from Roman Namur, is less organised and interesting. Much of the old city is beautiful, in a rather French style.
One of the 56 belfries in Belgium recognized as s.

x.intro: Namurs location at the head of the Ardennes has made it a popular tourist centre. The town's most prominent sight is the Citadel of Namur, now demilitarised and open to the public. Namur also has a distinctive 18th-century cathedral dedicated to Saint Aubain and a belfry classified by UNESCO as part of the Belfries of Belgium and France which are listed as a World Heritage Site. It has a casino in its southern district on the left bank of the Meuse.

must.d: The primary tourist attraction of Namur, the Citadel is a fortress at the confluence of the Meuse and Sambre rivers. Its original design dates from Roman times, with foundations laid out in 937.

next.d: the national capital
the Detroit of Wallonia with a rich industrial history

intro: A low-lying country in the Benelux, Belgium (Dutch: België, French: Belgique, German: Belgien) sits at the crossroads of Western Europe. It marries the historical landmarks for which the continent is famous with spectacular modern architecture and rural idylls. Its capital, Brussels, is home to the headquarters of the European Union.

other.d: a municipality with a rich industrial history on the outskirts of Brussels with many historical landmarks.

x.around: Modern Kraainem has a strongly residential outlook with a well developed road network. It has been completely mapped on OpenStreetMap, which is likely more up to date than the official maps offered by the tourist office.

hidden.d: The Cité, built between 1920 and 1923, was envisioned as a social residential complex for veterans from the First World War who returned from the front line with disabilities.
Before 1930, the area of the current cemetery existed as garden for the castle park of Edward De Burbure of Wezembeek.
A modern theater hall, grown into the cultural centre of Kraainem. New shows on a weekly basis. An opportunity for tourists to get a taste of Flemish culture and lifestyle.

The football club of Kraainem is known for its multiculturalism, uniting over 300 players from 40 countries in sports. Aside from 2 senior teams, the club is carried by youngsters between 6 and 21 years old.
The order of the Salesians was founded in 1610 close to Annecy in France by Jeanne de Chantal and Francis of Sales, who gave his name to the order.
Well preserved remains of the first residential activities in High Kraainem, dating from a Frankish settlement in the 9th century.

Memorial site for the local casualties of the two world wars. The square and its monument were constructed in 1930 when the adjacent Queen Astrid Avenue was conceived as the connection between High Kraainem and Stokkel.
A vicarage built in 1652 with a foundation of sandstone and red bricks. The characteristic arc door and slate roof, typical for the era it was built in, have survived restoration efforts.

x.intro: Kraainem is a municipality on the outskirts of the Brussels Capital Region, administratively belonging to Flemish Brabant. It began as a rural village, but the expansion of Brussels has led to a fast-paced urbanization of Kraainem throughout the 20th century, and the municipality has become a popular residence for Eurocrats and expats alike.

must.d: The Sonian Forest, covering an area of ca. 4400 ha, is the largest and best preserved remnant of the historical Silva Carbonaria, commonly known as the charcoal forest, that in the 4th century still stretched from Thuin to…
The oldest building in Kraainem, the Saint Pancras Church has its origins in the 12th century. The massive Roman tower with walls up to 1.7 meters thick most likely had a military function.

next.d: the capital of Belgium and host of many of the European Union institutions.
famous for beer, technology, and one of the oldest universities in Western Europe. Well preserved historic city centre.
the "green lung" of Brussels, known for its century-old beech trees.
a picturesque town in the shadow of the Sonian Forest with a large public park and former summer residence palace of the Belgian king.
famous for its abbey and beer.

x.safe: Kraainem is usually safe, both during the day and at night. The dangerous Belgian traffic probably poses the most significant risk to visitors, so take care when crossing streets. Jaywalking is not a criminal offence in Belgium, but that does not mean drivers will slow down either, unless you're crossing on a marked pedestrian crossing. Beware of pickpockets in shopping areas and on public transport.

other.d: known for its proximity to the lush Sonian Forest, its parks, and royal summer residence.

x.around: The town and adjacent park for which it is famous are easily explorable by foot. In winter, the dolomite-covered park tracks can remain wet from rain for a long time, so water resistant shoes are strongly recommended. Although rare, snow is not unseen in Tervuren, although it usually melts within a day or two.

hidden.d: Sculpture of an African elephant with raised trunk and three African warriors on its back, of which one is carrying a spear.

x.intro: Tervuren is a municipality in Flemish Brabant on the outskirts of the vast Sonian Forest, south-west of Brussels. It is best known as the host town of the Belgian king's summer residence, which is now the Museum for Central Africa, and for the beautiful park surrounding it.

must.d: Housed in the former summer palace of the Belgian kings. It is a centre for knowledge and resources on Africa, in particular Central Africa, in an historical, contemporary, and global context.

A command bunker part of the K-W Line (Koningshooikt - Wavre), built in 1939 to reinforce the existing defense line along the Albert canal and Meuse river, as an additional defense against a possible German invasion.
Designed for the World's Fair of 1897 by French architect Alfred-Philibert Aldrophe and finished by Enrest Acker as part of an exposition to justify the Belgian occupation of Congo.

next.d: the capital of Belgium and host of many of the European Union institutions.
neighbouring town with rich cultural and industrial heritage dating back to the 12th century.
famous for beer, technology, and one of the oldest universities in Western Europe. Well preserved historic city centre.

other.d: known for the beer with the same name, risen to worldwide fame, but still produced in its abbey.

x.around: There are no bike rental companies in Grimbergen. If you do need to rent a bike, the best option is to rent one in neighboring Vilvoorde and cycle to Grimbergen. The center of Vilvoorde is only 4km away.

hidden.d: Situated behind the Prinsenkasteel, the building used to be a stable and coach-house of the castle. The 1681 Renaissance building now houses the Museum of the Old Techniques and some exhibition rooms.

A wellness oasis with extensive sauna and bathing facilities, both indoor and outdoor. Enjoy the steam bath, hammam, whirlpool, jacuzzi, swimming pools and numerous saunas and relaxation rooms close to the historic centre of…

The oldest part of this castle date back to the 15th and 16th century. After intensive reparation works in the 17th century due to war damage the castle was expanded and rebuilt once again in the 19th century.
Explore a gigantic interactive map of the sky, try out different experiments, view telescopes and a meteorological office. Who knows, you may even make your own discovery!
One of the four water mills on the Maalbeek stream in Grimbergen. This mill was named after the family Van Oyenbrugghe. The mill was mentioned for the first time in 1397.
16th-century watermill along the Maalbeek stream. Just like the Liermolen a part of the Museum of the Old Techniques is also located in this mill. Another barn is now used as a rural tavern.
Small chapel built in 1734. It is located on the corner of Guldendal and Prinsenstraat.

Grimbergen's main trade mark is its beer, which is sold all over Belgium and even abroad. The museum is located in a 17th-century abbey farm and was the first of its kind in Belgium. Visits only can be made after a reservation.

x.intro: Grimbergen is a town of 37,000 inhabitants (2018) in Flemish Brabant, Belgium, just north of Brussels. The town is known for its abbey, castles and abbey beer.

must.d: Baroque basilica built between 1660 and 1725. It is richly adorned with exceptional wooden sculptures made by Flemish artist of that time. The church tower has a carillon.

next.d: the thriving national capital is nearby.
compact historical city northeast of Grimbergen.
a municipality with a rich industrial history to the southeast of Grimbergen.
an oasis of nature and peace to the south of Brussels.

other.d: small city in a stunning natural setting, a popular spot for adventure sports such as canoeing and rock-climbing, best visited in winter

x.around: No need to take public transport at all since Dinant is a very small town and the main tourist sites are within walking distance.

hidden.d: Leffe is a popular beer in Belgium and it originated in Dinant. The former abbey beer is no longer made in Dinant, but in this museum you can learn all about the origins of the beer, the life of the monks and the actual Leffe,…
Finished in 1923, 1,104 French soldiers are buried here who died during battles in the Dinant region between 15 and 23 August 1914.
Wellness centre with warm baths, saunas, lounge, terrace and garden. Free private parking space.

This cave was discovered in 1904 and is one of the most beautiful ones in Belgium. There are small waterfalls inside the cave. A visit to the beautiful caves is highly recommended. They are easy to visit.

x.intro: Dinant is a relatively small but very picturesque city in the province of Namur in Belgium. It stretches along the river Meuse against the steep rock face behind on the eastern side, with a thinner strip on the western side against a forest. Its old town is perhaps one of the most impressive sights in Wallonia, but the locality is relatively remote.

must.d: The church dominating the city's riverbank stands in the place where a previous Romanesque one was destroyed by rocks falling from the cliff in 1227.
Located in the neighbourhood of Leffe north of the Citadel, the abbey has been inhabited since 1152 and features a splendid organ.

n.es: Abadía de Nuestra Señora de Leffe

must.d: On a cliff, more than 100 m above the River Meuse, it offers spectacular views of the town and countryside. A fortification may have stood on this spot as long ago as the fourth century, and the Bishop Prince of Liège certainly…
The house of Monsieur Sax contains a small interpretation centre on the inventor of the saxophone. A life-size statue of the inventor sits on a bench in front of the house.

The 40-m-tall rock needle at the Meuse riverbank according to the local legend been separated from the main rock mass by the strike of the hoof by Bayard, the magical horse carrying the four sons of Duke Ayman on the run from…

next.d: You probably have to go through this city on your way to Dinant. This provincial capital is worth some time as well.

x.safe: Being the relaxed small town it is, Dinant does not pose any major danger to travellers.

other.d: also called the "Tuscany of the north", is a green region west of Brussels, consisting of rolling hills, meadows, small villages and castles.

x.intro: Flemish Brabant is one of the five provinces of Flanders (Belgium). The province completely surrounds Brussels, the national capital. Brussels however is not a part of the province. The capital Leuven is one of Belgium's largest student cities. The university is one of the oldest universities in this part of Europe and makes the city one with an impressive student tradition.

other.d: the hot water treatments of the spa town that gave its name to all spas in the world has drawn visitors for centuries.

x.around: The centre of Spa is relatively small, but many attractions are in farther villages and neighbouring municipalities. TEC runs a network of bus lines connecting them.

hidden.d: The city museum collects artifacts of the history of Spa with focus on its springs and related developments. It is housed in a villa that was built for the Belgian queen Marie-Henriette in 1863.

Spa's emblematic building houses the mineral water fountain named after the Russian Tsar Peter the Great, who visited the city in the 18th century and became a big fan of its healing and wellness qualities.
Venue of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix, and of the Spa 24 Hours and 1000 km Spa endurance races. The next F1 races are 23-25 July 2027.
Wellness centre on top of the hill in the town.
This ancient-looking church was built to follow late Roman style prevalent in the region closely, but was in fact built in 1885.

other.d: and surrounding villages — destroyed during World War I, this former military stronghold is marked by memorials and cemeteries.

x.around: For visiting the war graves and memorials, one could use a car or cycle. Take the guided "Battle field tour" - bus, or buy an audio tour on the internet - same sites, but a lot cheaper if you have your own transport

hidden.d: Military cemetery in the town of Ypres with 198 Commonwealth soldiers buried next to the Lille Gate (Rijselpoort).
Museum in a beautiful setting, telling the story of the Great War in chronological order. Lots of information on the different battles and a large selection of authentic artifacts on display.

x.intro: Ypres (Dutch: Ieper, both pronounced "eeper") is a friendly town of 35,000 inhabitants in Flanders endowed with wonderful architecture and a troubled past. Ypres is best known as the site of three major battles of the First World War, the most famous being the Battle of Passchendaele from July to November 1917. The many memorials and cemeteries of the fallen in and around Ypres draw thousands of visitors each year. The belfry of Ypres is a .

must.d: Dedicated on 24 July 1927 as a memorial to the missing British and Commonwealth soldiers who fell in Belgium during World War One.

The largest Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery in the world, situated to the south of the village of Passchendaele. There's a massive wall at the back of the cemetery, containing names of many missing soldiers.

n.fr: cimetière militaire britannique de Tyne Cot

must.d: This museum gives an excellent overview of World War I. It is more like an experience that takes you right into daily life during the war.
A well-preserved World War I battle site that changed sides repeatedly. There area covered in craters. There was also a large amount of tunneling during the war which adds to the uneven terrain.
One of the most important German cemeteries from the First World War lies in the village of Vladslo, north of Ypres and close to the city of Diksmuide.
The cemetery, which evolved from a small group of graves in 1915, has seen numerous changes and extensions. It was dedicated in 1932. Today, visitors find a mass grave near the entrance.

next.d: is the closest city reachable by rail. Kortrijk is a nice provincial city offering history or shopping and has important rail connections to Brussels, Ghent, Bruges, Antwerp, Lille.
Diksmuide, Poperinge and Menin.

x.safe: Ypres is generally very safe. Pickpockets are rare, and violence is very rare. Do watch out in the streets where there's busy traffic.

other.d: known for its market square (the largest in Belgium), its annual balloon festival and nearby scenery along the river Scheldt.

hidden.d: Nice park with castle surrounded by a moat.
The city's main square is Belgium's largest market square, almost rivals Moscow's Red Square and the Vatican's St.Peter's Square in size.

x.intro: Sint-Niklaas is a medium-sized city (by Belgian standards) of around 82,000 people (2023), in East Flanders, between the bigger cities of Antwerp and Ghent. It is the capital city of the Waas region (Waasland), which is surrounded by the river Schelde (Scheldt) on three sides.

next.d: The most interesting nearby city to visit (besides Antwerp and Ghent of course) is Hulst in the Netherlands, just across the border, 15 km to the north of Sint-Niklaas.
